edges.description: The DPH1-DPH2 heterodimer catalyses the first committed step of diphthamide biosynthesis, so reduced DPH1 activity reduces flux through the whole four-step pathway.
Structural work places diphthamide in the ribosomal decoding centre, where it contacts mRNA and rRNA; without it, reading-frame maintenance degrades.

edges.description: The neural crest link is established by conditional deletion in mouse rather than by a measured fidelity defect in human craniofacial tissue, so the edge is indirect.

No source traces a path from reduced translational accuracy to growth restriction or to the neurodevelopmental deficit, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown rather than the edge being asserted as direct.

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic DPH1 variants reduce the activity of the DPH1 subunit of the DPH1-DPH2 heterodimer. Reduction rather than abolition is the rule: complete inactivation of diphthamide synthesis is embryonic or perinatally lethal in animals, so a living affected individual necessarily retains residual activity.

evidence.snippet: In all cases, diphthamide synthesis of the homozygous or compound heterozygous carriers of variant alleles appeared to be reduced but not completely abolished.

nodes.description: The DPH1-DPH2 iron-sulfur heterodimer, with electrons donated by DPH3 and DPH4, converts histidine 715 of human eEF2 to a 3-amino-3-carboxypropyl intermediate; DPH5, DPH7 and DPH6 then complete the modification. Reduced first-step activity leaves eEF2 under-modified at this single residue. eEF2 is non-redundant, so there is no parallel pathway to compensate.

evidence.snippet: An iron-sulfur (FeS) cluster containing DPH1/DPH2 heterodimer that needs DPH3/DPH4 for electron donation generates 3-amino-3-carboxypropyl (ACP)-modified histidine at position His715 of human eEF2.

evidence.snippet: We summarized previously reported patients in the literature and found that developmental delay, unusual skull shape, sparse hair, and facial dysmorphism were consistently present in all DPH1 syndrome patients.

nodes.description: Cranial neural crest derivatives are disproportionately affected, which is the developmental account of the skull shape and facial features. Mouse conditional deletion of Dph1 restricted to neural crest produces hypoplastic nasal bone and lower jaw, and the gene lies within the Miller-Dieker critical deletion region, which is what prompted that experiment.

evidence.snippet: Expression of transgenic myc-tagged Ovca1 in craniofacial structures can partially rescue the cleft palate and shortened mandible of Ovca1-null embryos.

nodes.description: Diphthamide-deficient cells sit with oxidative-stress and NF-kappaB transcriptional programs partly engaged before any exogenous stress, and are hypersensitive to oxidative challenge and to tumour-necrosis-factor-mediated death signalling. This is a cell-level consequence demonstrated in engineered human lines, not a measurement made in patient tissue.

nodes.description: Bulk protein synthesis continues, but elongation becomes error-prone and permits -1 frameshifting. Loss of diphthamide also lowers selenocysteine incorporation at recoded SECIS-UGA codons and shifts tRNA synthetase expression, so the consequence is a reweighted proteome rather than a global translational arrest. This distinguishes the disease from ribosomopathies that limit ribosome production.

biological_processes: maintenance of translational reading frame during elongation

Central nervous system malformations and early lethality were more frequent in this family than in the founder cohort.

nodes.description: Homozygous deep intronic variant in a sibling pair who had carried a clinical diagnosis of Fine-Lubinsky syndrome for years. Chromosomal microarray and quad exome sequencing were both non-diagnostic; a research reanalysis found the variant, and RNA sequencing on fibroblasts showed markedly reduced DPH1 transcript consistent with abnormal splicing followed by nonsense-mediated decay. The practical lesson is that this allele class is invisible to a standard exome pipeline, so a negative exome does not exclude the diagnosis.

nodes.description: Two further missense alleles whose function was measured directly, in four new patients from two families. Both reduce DPH1 activity in the diphtheria-toxin ADP-ribosylation assay, placing them with p.Leu234Pro, p.Leu164Pro and the p.Ala411Argfs*91 frameshift among the five of seven tested alleles shown to be functionally compromised. Grouped in one record because the source reports them as a set within one functional series and does not separate their phenotypic effects.
